statutory.question: Does the conduct described fall within 31 U.S.C. § 5324 — Structuring transactions to evade reporting requirements?
statutory.answer: No. § 5324 prohibits structuring to evade reporting requirements, but the facts do not show transactions structured around the $10,000 CTR threshold or an intent to evade reporting.
statutory.label: neutral
statutory.reasoning: 31 U.S.C. § 5324 makes it unlawful to (a)(1) cause or attempt to cause a domestic financial institution to fail to file a required report, (a)(2) cause or attempt to cause a domestic financial institution to file a report containing a material omission/misstatement, or (a)(3) structure/assist in structuring (or attempt) any transaction with one or more domestic financial institutions for the purpose of evading the reporting requirements of 31 U.S.C. § 5313(a) (CTR reporting, generally triggered by cash transactions >$10,000 in a single day). Here, the fact pattern shows multiple cash transactions (many individually above $10,000, e.g., $14,726.29; $16,212.41; $17,978.06; $20,087.87) rather than repeated sub-$10,000 cash deposits/withdrawals that would suggest structuring to avoid CTRs; such >$10,000 cash transactions would ordinarily be reportable rather than evasive. The record also includes card/ACH/wire payments, which generally are not CTR-triggering cash transactions under § 5313(a), and there is no evidence of same-day aggregation across multiple cash transactions being deliberately kept below $10,000, no evidence any bank report was avoided or falsified, and no stated purpose/intent to evade reporting. Because § 5324 requires a purpose to evade reporting (and/or causing a failure or falsity in required reports), the provided facts are insufficient to conclude the conduct falls within § 5324.
